findings.text: follow-on: this extraction re-implements the pytest failure-id diff that reckon/crew/review.py:2100 added_failures_from_gate_logs already owns for exactly this base-versus-head comparison; calling the owner would have carried its format guard and its per-arm working-directory reduction, and the hand-rolled form does neither.

follow-on: the pipeline greps each arm log without checking that the file exists or that grep matched, so an absent or truncated log yields empty base-fails.txt and cand-fails.txt and a reported added=0 that is indistinguishable from the measured zero; the logs are present here and the positive control covers the parse, so the result stands, but the harness would not redden when its input vanished.

item_verdicts.diff: the node committed nothing (git -C <its worktree> rev-parse HEAD returns d0d0d28c4, git status -uno clean), so there is no product diff to read, consistent with its brief stating it changes no product code and commits nothing.
item_verdicts.done_when: the source brief's evidence fence requires each arm's log to start with the revision, host and literal command, print reckon.__file__ under the arm's own checkout, and end in EXIT=; arm-base.log and arm-candidate.log each carry all four (heads, cwd:/module: at :10-11, EXIT=0 at the tail).
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to measure the review-dispatch importer population of the confined review-record grant at base and at its merge candidate on an exclusive node; run 1287898 on host 98dci4-clu-3144 ran one pytest arm at each revision over the 63-file population in /home/ITER/mcintos/.cache/reckon-population-lists/review-record-grant.txt, which is that measurement.
item_verdicts.manifest: read in full; it records status complete, commits none, both arms' pass/fail counts and log paths, the 63-file population with no file absent at base, zero added failing ids with alone-summary.txt empty for that reason, the positive control, and two attributed scaffolding retry_failures.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the source node declared one write path, the report directory under crew/reports/reckon/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home/review-record-grant-population-at-merge, plus the run directory its host line grants; every changed path lies in one of the two and no path under reckon/ or tests/ was written.

justifications.durability: the measured zero is reproducible from the two arm logs through reckon/crew/review.py:2100, but the node added no guard, and population-job.sh:100-102 checks neither that the arm logs exist nor that grep matched, so a missing log would yield added=0 indistinguishable from the measured zero.
justifications.evidence: I re-derived the added-failure claim by calling reckon/crew/review.py:2100 added_failures_from_gate_logs on arm-base.log and arm-candidate.log, which returned (0, []), and control-before/after.log show the same parse reporting a failure it was given; the deduction is that population-job.sh:100-103 derives the claim by hand rather than through that owner, and silently reports added=0 when an arm log is unreadable.
justifications.fit: a naming sweep over report.md and population-job.sh returns no plan labels, deliverable IDs, ticket references or AI attribution, and the job and its arms are named by what they are (arm-base.log, arm-candidate.log, run_arm).
justifications.goal_fidelity: population-job.sh:78-81 runs run_arm for base and candidate and the two arm logs under /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261017T070403824277-review-record-grant-population-at-merge report files_run: 63 on each.
justifications.reuse: population-job.sh:100-102 hand-rolls the FAILED/ERROR extraction and comm diff that reckon/crew/review.py:2100 added_failures_from_gate_logs already owns, without calling or extending it, so the landed extraction forks a capability the repository owns.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path in the manifest is inside the declared report directory or the host-granted run directory, and the reviewed worktree at d0d0d28c4 is clean with reckon/ and tests/ untouched.
